newsitem.title: USA: Albright expects "good news" on Korea peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Albright expects "good news" on Korea peace talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Wednesday she expected there might be "good news" from talks in New York on long-term peace in the Korean peninsula.
"We expect that we in fact might have some good news about the North Koreans' acceptance of four-party talks that deal with the Korean peninsula," Albright said.
Albright was answering questions from the audience after giving a speech at the rededication of the Gerald R. Ford Museum in Grand Rapids, Michigan.
A State Department spokesman in Washington had already reported early progress at the New York meeting of delegations from the United States, North Korea and South Korea.

The meeting is aimed at securing participation by the Stalinist North Korean government in four-party talks, also including China, to work for a Korean peace treaty to replace the fraying armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
The spokesman in Washington had said it was likely all three participants would make statements at the end of the talks, which he expected would be later on Wednesday.
